title: MDISCO: A High-Throughput Tissue-Clearing Protocol for Mouse Brains
author: Madeline Martinez
license_note: PMC full-text XML — Bio-protocol — CC-BY confirmed in article XML
materials: B6.Cg- Gt(ROSA)26Sor tm9(CAG-tdTomato)Hze /J mice [Jackson Laboratory, strain #007909; common name: Ai9 or Ai9(RCL-tdT)] [7]
STOCK Fos tm2.1(icre/ERT2)Luo /J mice [Jackson Laboratory, strain #030323, common name: Fos 2A-iCreER (TRAP2)] [8]
B6.129(Cg)- Oprl1 tm1.1Mrbr /J mice (gifted from the Bruchas Lab at the University of Washington, Jackson Laboratory, strain #036308, common name: NOPR loxP/YFP ) [10] Reagents

steps.title: Anesthetize mouse
steps.instruction: Anesthetize the mouse according to approved institutional animal care protocols.

steps.title: Perfuse with PBS
steps.instruction: Perfuse transcardially with 20–30 mL of 1× PBS at ~5–10 mL/min until the liver clears.

steps.title: Perfuse with 4% PFA
steps.instruction: Prepare fresh 4% (w/v) PFA in PBS by dissolving PFA powder in 1× PBS at 60 °C, adding 1 M NaOH dropwise, adjusting pH to 7.4, cooling, and filtering through a 0.45 µm filter. Immediately perfuse with 20–30 mL of this solution at the same flow rate.

steps.title: Dissect and post‑fix brain
steps.instruction: Dissect the brain carefully, immerse it in 10–15 mL of 4% PFA to ensure complete submersion, and fix overnight at 4 °C with gentle agitation if possible.

steps.title: PBS wash at 37 °C
steps.instruction: Transfer the fixed brain to a clean container containing 1× PBS and incubate overnight at 37 °C with rocking if possible.

steps.title: Inspect and clean brain
steps.instruction: Inspect the sample and remove any hair or debris from the brain surface.

steps.title: Methanol dehydration series
steps.instruction: Transfer the brain sequentially through MeOH/water (v/v) gradients—20%, 40%, 60%, 80% MeOH—each for 1 h at room temperature (RT), then incubate in 100% MeOH for 1 h at RT, replace with fresh 100% MeOH and incubate overnight at RT (samples may be stored in 100% MeOH).

steps.title: Delipidation with DCM/MeOH
steps.instruction: Transfer the brain to 66% dichloromethane (DCM) / 33% methanol (MeOH) in a solvent‑resistant container and incubate overnight at RT with rocking.

steps.title: MeOH wash before bleaching
steps.instruction: Wash the brain in 100% MeOH for 2 h at RT, then replace with fresh 100% MeOH and incubate an additional 2 h at RT.

steps.title: Prepare fresh 6% H₂O₂/MeOH
steps.instruction: Just before use, mix 1 part 30% H₂O₂ with 4 parts MeOH to obtain a 6% H₂O₂ solution in MeOH.

steps.title: Bleach brain overnight
steps.instruction: Incubate the brain in the freshly prepared 6% H₂O₂/MeOH solution overnight at 4 °C. Always prepare fresh solution; old peroxide increases background.

steps.title: Post‑bleach MeOH wash
steps.instruction: Wash the brain in 100% MeOH for 1 h at RT, then replace with fresh 100% MeOH and incubate overnight at RT.

steps.title: Final DCM/MeOH incubation
steps.instruction: Incubate the brain in 66% DCM / 33% MeOH for 3 h at RT.

steps.title: Incubate in 100% DCM
steps.instruction: Replace the solution with 100% DCM and incubate for 1 h at RT.

steps.title: Transfer to DBE
steps.instruction: Transfer the brain to 100% dibenzyl ether (DBE) and rock at RT until the tissue becomes cleared (typically several hours).

steps.title: DBE incubation for bubble removal
steps.instruction: Keep the brain in DBE for 4–5 days to allow internal bubbles to dissipate fully; optionally place in a 37 °C incubator and check hourly to accelerate bubble removal.

steps.title: Replace DBE with ECi
steps.instruction: Once bubbles are eliminated and the tissue appears optically uniform, replace DBE with ethyl cinnamate (ECi) for final refractive‑index matching and storage.

description: Validation of protocol To validate the performance and reproducibility of the MDISCO clearing protocol, tissue morphology, optical transparency, and endogenous fluorescence preservation were quantitatively compared with FDISCO+ [6]. As shown in Figure 1 , both clearing methods produced measurable changes in brain morphology relative to the PBS baseline. MDISCO- and FDISCO+-cleared brains exhibited comparable changes in anteroposterior (AP) length, with no statistically significant difference between methods. In contrast, mediolateral (ML) shrinkage was significantly reduced in MDISCO-cleared samples relative to FDISCO+, indicating improved preservation of lateral tissue dimensions. Brain weight changes followed a similar trend, with MDISCO showing reduced variability across samples. Consistent with prior reports indicating that peroxide formation in DBE at room temperature contributes to endogenous fluorescence decay, prolonged exposure to DBE was avoided in this protocol [6]. Optical transparency, quantified as normalized light transmittance, was significantly increased in MDISCO-cleared brains compared to FDISCO+, reflecting more uniform refractive index matching and reduced residual scattering. Although the FDISCO+ protocol was implemented repeatedly with careful pH control, recommended antioxidant additives, and early transfer to ECi, its performance was variable and consistently inferior to MDISCO under our experimental conditions, highlighting the sensitivity of THF-based workflows to experimental context. Fluorescence preservation was evaluated to assess the robustness and reproducibility of the MDISCO clearing protocol. All images were acquired using a Miltenyi UltraMicroscope Blaze II light-sheet microscope with identical acquisition settings applied across samples within each fluorophore group to control for imaging-related variability.
